parallel.requirements: Recognized the clean-room requirement, no source lookup or wrapping, and the need to match the provided goimports-reviser CLI through observed behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent retained broad ownership while spawning four child activities for CLI probing and rewrite behavior; children also wrote implementation artifacts in the shared workspace.
parallel.implementation: Built a root-level Go implementation across main.go, config.go, imports.go, packageinfo.go, and processor.go, with explicit parsing, import grouping, aliasing, traversal, and output handling.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated child findings and code, but a child rebuilt the shared ./executable early; the parent later repaired go.mod and compile.sh before the final GO111MODULE=off build.
parallel.verification: Ran side-by-side behavioral fixture checks for help/version, output modes, recursive traversal, excludes, generated files, import grouping, rm-unused, aliases, and exit status.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite broader coverage and a higher score than serial, the final replacement still failed 158 official tests and retained many probe artifacts in the submitted tree.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room constraints and used only documentation plus CLI interaction with the bundled executable.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor handled probing, implementation, build-script changes, verification, and final delivery without delegation or cross-agent handoff.
serial.implementation: Built a compact Go implementation in cmd/executable/main.go with compile.sh, initially added a root go.mod, then removed it after finding a project-detection regression.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Final delivery consisted of cmd/executable/main.go plus compile.sh and a rebuilt ./executable, with no multi-agent merge or workspace ownership conflict.
serial.verification: Used command-driven checks against the earlier probe matrix for representative single-file, directory, generated-file, project-name, invalid-flag, and exit-code cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The implementation remained behaviorally incomplete against the official evaluator, failing 195 official tests and adding no separate automated test suite.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel accepted the clean-room reverse-engineering constraints and targeted an original executable matching observed CLI behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial accepted the same clean-room constraints and also worked from CLI/documentation observations rather than source lookup.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-understanding split is visible; both failures reflect incomplete behavioral fidelity, not a different stated task.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed by spawning multiple children while the parent kept final integration responsibility.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one local trajectory with no subagents or delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created cross-agent ownership boundaries over probing, implementation, and final workspace state; serial avoided those boundaries entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs are mostly encrypted in raw logs, but visible spawn and handoff evidence show children working against the same workspace and executable path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept requirements, observations, code, and verification in one actor, so there was no child interface contract to preserve.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The key interface difference was not missing task context; it was shared workspace and deliverable ownership across agents.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delivered a multi-file root-level Go implementation with helper modules for configuration, imports, package info, and processing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial delivered a single main implementation under cmd/executable plus compile.sh.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced a broader and better-scoring implementation, but both implementations missed official cases and failed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received a child final answer and continued parent-side repair and finalization afterward.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial closed its own plan locally after implementation, build correction, and representative verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel did not lose a completed child result, but the child result arrived with a workspace side effect that the parent had to manage; serial had no result join boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: A child built into the shared ./executable, and the parent later noted that the original observation binary had been replaced.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial detected its own root go.mod regression and changed compile.sh in the same actor before rebuilding.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel suffered a cross-agent deliverable/provenance overwrite; serial performed similar cleanup without concurrent ownership conflict.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel reported a broad manual behavior matrix and post-rebuild checks, but not enough evaluator-aligned coverage for a pass.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reported representative command-driven checks and no separate automated test suite.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verified more cases and achieved a higher score, but both accepted without official-equivalent completeness.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 1297.901 agent seconds, 17.4M tokens, and four subagents before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 725.06 agent seconds, 3.28M tokens, and zero subagents before closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed substantially more budget but still completed; the retained issue is the deliverable overwrite, not standalone budget exhaustion.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: parallel and serial both failed. Parallel passed more tests, apparently because its broader probing and multi-file implementation covered more CLI and rewriting behavior, but the evidence does not support claiming a pass/fail causal split.
parallel_contributors: Broader parallel probing and a larger root-level implementation covered more observed cases and scored higher.
The child deliverable overwrite created a real repair/provenance burden before closure.
serial_contributors: Serial kept implementation and build cleanup within one actor, avoiding cross-agent state collision.
Serial's compact implementation and representative-only verification left more official cases failing.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both solutions were incomplete clean-room approximations of goimports-reviser behavior.
Parallel kept more probe artifacts in the final tree, while serial's artifact tree was simpler.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported comparative process and coverage explanation only

The parent owned the end-to-end probe, implementation, repair, rebuild, and final response pipeline.
Implementation and probing overlapped; productive work was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight gate.
The parent implemented and patched while children probed, rather than deferring all implementation until after an investigation phase.
The indispensable implementation path received parent and child effort and completed a deliverable; no specific starved path is shown.
Parallel used high tokens and four children, but completed without timeout; the concrete adverse event is the write collision, not exhausted budget.
No single child is shown receiving an overbroad task that it failed to checkpoint; the problematic child completed and wrote the deliverable.
Visible evidence does not show a known task, environment, or delivery requirement omitted from a child brief and then followed incorrectly.
The observed failure is not incompatible independently produced components; it is a concrete overwrite of the shared executable path.
No known finding is shown disappearing through summary or transfer; the parent received and acted on child output.
Child returns were available and used; there is no decision window where excessive handoff volume prevented consumption.
The parent did not rely on superseded child state as current; it noticed the changed executable and repaired workspace state.
No incompatible child reports remained unadjudicated at closure; the concrete conflict is represented by the write label.
The parent ran post-repair checks and did not declare completion solely from workflow status or file existence; evaluator failure alone cannot supply this label.

The child implementation was retrievable and effectively joined into the final workspace; the parent later adjusted and rebuilt it.

The parent received the completed cli_probe result and used its implications when repairing the workspace.
The parent did not wait until timeout without inspection; it continued active probing, patching, result receipt, repair, and rebuild.
Agents did work across files, but the proven adverse event is the concrete replacement of the executable deliverable.
The same chain included compile.sh edits, but the higher-precedence and realized boundary is replacement of ./executable.
The overwritten object that produced the process consequence was the required executable/oracle, not merely a non-entry source or config file.
A live child wrote and built into the shared required ./executable while the parent still owned final verification and had been using that path as the observation binary.

candidates.near_match_reason: Source/config edits were present in the same chain, but taxonomy precedence chooses the more specific required deliverable replacement.
